default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1178.title: EMA ribbon alignment onset
E-1178.hypothesis: When fast, medium and slow EMAs (n, 2n, 4n) line up with price above them for the first time, trend followers and slow hedgers keep adding in that direction; follow the onset.

E-1179.title: Net wick-pressure follow
E-1179.hypothesis: Persistent lower wicks over a window mean sellers are repeatedly absorbed by passive buyers (and vice versa); when the average wick imbalance crosses a threshold, trade with the absorbers.

E-1180.title: Z-score recovery through the mean
E-1180.hypothesis: After a stretch below (above) the rolling mean, the first close back through the mean shows the forced flow has ended; follow the return leg.

E-1181.title: Closing-hour VWAP stretch fade
E-1181.hypothesis: Near the close, benchmark-driven (VWAP) execution and position squaring pull price toward VWAP; fade a stretched price when a bar turns back toward it.

E-1182.title: Block staircase break
E-1182.hypothesis: Block lows rising three blocks in a row show steady passive demand; a close over the latest block high means supply is exhausted. Mirror for sellers.

E-1183.title: RSI centre-line recovery
E-1183.hypothesis: After RSI visits a weak zone and then crosses 50, momentum has flipped and the late shorts cover; follow the flip.

E-1184.title: Marubozu run follow
E-1184.hypothesis: Consecutive bars with bodies filling most of their range mean one side is hitting through the book with no pushback; follow.

E-1185.title: Short-window volume surge direction
E-1185.hypothesis: A sudden surge of volume over a few minutes versus the last hour signals informed or forced flow; the net price direction of the surge is the side that is winning.

E-1186.title: Rising bar-midpoint run
E-1186.hypothesis: Bar midpoints (high+low)/2 rising several bars in a row with the close above the midpoint show whole ranges migrating up, stronger than close-to-close runs; follow.

E-1187.title: Day-move t-statistic follow
E-1187.hypothesis: Normalising the move since the open by the typical bar volatility and sqrt(time) isolates drifts too persistent to be noise; follow when the t-statistic crosses a threshold.
